why: The paper releases no code (no repository, no code_links, no stated compute), so there is nothing to run as-is. The target claim C1 is a single L2-regularised logistic regression on a public 7,043-row tabular dataset with a standard sklearn pipeline (label/one-hot encoding, min-max scaling, SMOTE on the training partition only, stratified 80/20 split, fixed 0.5 threshold). That is cheap and fully specified in the claim contract and Table 1 config, so the cheapest faithful path is to reimplement the pipeline from the paper text and the claim contract rather than hunt for author artefacts.
est_runtime: about 6-10 minutes of command time: ~3 minutes to install scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn and pandas, ~1 minute to fetch the CSV, under 5 seconds to fit the logistic regression, and a few minutes for the 5-fold CV and the optional RF/XGB/LGBM comparison rows
blockers: no author repository or code link anywhere in the contract
Kaggle download requires an authenticated API token or a manual CSV drop; a mirror/alternative URL must be used if credentials are unavailable
Python 3.12 is fine for modern sklearn/imbalanced-learn, but historical library versions from the paper are not pinned, so exact bit-level reproduction of 0.8411 is not guaranteed
single 80/20 split means the reported AUC depends on the seed; only the 5-fold CV claim (C4, 0.845±0.013) is seed-robust

approach: No author code exists, so the plan reimplements the paper pipeline from the claim contract and targets C1 first: load and validate the IBM Telco CSV, apply the specified label/one-hot/min-max preprocessing, hold out a stratified 20% test set, apply SMOTE only to the training partition, fit the L2 logistic regression, and compute AUC-ROC on the untouched test set. The same pipeline is then reused for the cheap companion checks (5-fold CV, optional RF/XGBoost/LightGBM rows, top-risk quintile projection) so the output is a faithful reproduction rather than a hand-tuned one-off. SHAP/LIME, CRM tiering, and PSI monitoring are implemented as optional analysis because the match target is C1 and these should never block the headline result. Dataset acquisition is made robust by trying public CSV mirrors first, validating the 7,043 x 21 schema, and falling back to an explicit Kaggle-download error only if no mirror is reachable.
steps: Create results/ and data/ directories and install dependencies with python -m pip install -U numpy pandas scikit-learn imbalanced-learn requests shap lime xgboost lightgbm.

In data_utils.ensure_dataset(), try each configured public CSV URL with requests; write the first valid CSV to data/ and validate that it has 7043 rows and 21 columns. If no mirror works, attempt the Kaggle CLI only when credentials exist, otherwise raise a clear dataset-missing error.
Load the CSV with pandas, coerce TotalCharges to numeric and fill blank/NaN values with 0 per A1, verify the expected 21-column schema, drop customerID, and map Churn Yes/No to target 1/0.
Apply the R2 label encoding to gender, Partner, Dependents, PhoneService, and PaperlessBilling with Yes=1/No=0 and Male=1/Female=0; leave SeniorCitizen unchanged.

Sandeep Gaddamwar

Abstract—Subscriber attrition is a costly, persistent challenge for telecommunications providers, with monthly churn of roughly 1.9%
in mature markets eroding billions in revenue annually. Predictive models can flag at-risk customers accurately, yet they are routinely
excluded from frontline CRM workflows because high-performing ensemble and non-linear architectures are opaque: a retention spe-
cialist cannot design a personalised intervention from a probability score alone, without knowing why a subscriber is at risk. This paper
addresses that gap. We benchmark four classifiers—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM—on the IBM Telco
Customer Churn benchmark (7,043 records; 19 features; 26.5% churn, balanced to 50% via SMOTE on the training partition only).
Logistic Regression attains the strongest AUC-ROC (0.8411) and LightGBM the highest accuracy (78.42%); all four fall within a 0.011
AUC band (0.831–0.841), and 5-fold cross-validation confirms the leading models are effectively tied. Explanations are delivered at two
granularities: a global SHAP ranking identifying tenure, total charges, and month-to-month contract as the dominant churn signals, and
instance-level SHAP and LIME decompositions that expose the drivers behind each prediction. Building on these outputs, we introduce
a four-layer CRM integration architecture that converts risk scores and attribution vectors into tiered segmentation, maps top features to
structured retention-action templates, and routes campaign outcomes into a retraining feedback loop. Targeting the highest-risk quintile
is projected to cut overall churn by 3.3–5.3 percentage points, preserving an estimated $199K–$319K per campaign cycle.
Index Terms—explainable AI, customer churn prediction, SHAP, LIME, gradient boosting, telecom analytics, CRM integration, im-
balanced learning, retention management.

Retaining subscribers is, on almost every financial metric,
preferable to acquiring new ones. The commonly cited ratio of
acquisition-to-retention cost sits between four and seven times,
depending on market maturity and competitive intensity [1].
Against this backdrop, voluntary churn—a subscriber’s decision
to terminate service and move to a competitor—represents a di-
rect, measurable revenue loss with a well-understood economic
structure. An operator losing 1,000 subscribers per month at an
average monthly revenue of $65 is foregoing $780,000 annu-
ally from that cohort alone, before accounting for downstream

def _valid_csv(path):
    try:
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
    except Exception:
        return False
    return df.shape == (C.EXPECTED_ROWS, C.EXPECTED_COLUMNS)


def ensure_dataset(verbose=True):
    """Return a path to a validated 7043 x 21 copy of the IBM Telco CSV.

    Order: shared download cache -> local data/ -> public mirrors.
    """
    os.makedirs(C.LOCAL_DATA_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cand = _cache_path()
    if cand and os.path.exists(cand) and _valid_csv(cand):
        if not os.path.exists(C.RAW_CSV):
            shutil.copyfile(cand, C.RAW_CSV)
        return C.RAW_CSV
    if os.path.exists(C.RAW_CSV) and _valid_csv(C.RAW_CSV):
        return C.RAW_CSV

    last_err = None
    for url in C.CANDIDATE_URLS:
        try:
            if verbose:
                print(f"[data] downloading {url}")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as resp:
                blob = resp.read()
            if cand:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cand), exist_ok=True)
                with open(cand, "wb") as fh:

            with open(C.RAW_CSV, "wb") as fh:
                fh.write(blob)

import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score,

)
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler

import config as C
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ metrics
def auc_trapezoid(y_true, y_score):
    """AUC-ROC by explicit trapezoidal integration of the ROC curve (R11)."""
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_true, y_score)
    return float(np.trapezoid(tpr, fpr))


def evaluate(y_true, y_score, threshold=C.THRESHOLD):
    y_pred = (np.asarray(y_score) >= threshold).astype(int)
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    return {
        "n": int(len(y_true)),
        "threshold": float(threshold),
        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "auc_roc": float(roc_auc_score(y_true, y_score)),
        "auc_roc_trapezoid": auc_trapezoid(y_true, y_score),
        "confusion": {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)},
    }


def majority_baseline(y_train, y_test):
    pred = int(np.round(np.mean(y_train)))
    acc = float(np.mean(np.asarray(y_test) == pred))
    return {"majority_class": pred, "accuracy": acc}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ models
def fit_logistic_regression(X, y, seed=C.SEED):
    params = dict(C.LR_PARAMS)
    params["random_state"] = seed
    model = LogisticRegression(**params)
    model.fit(X, y)

def fit_random_forest(X, y, seed=C.SEED):

    params = dict(C.RF_PARAMS)

    model.fit(X, y)
    return model

    return model

    from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier

    model = LGBMClassifier(random_state=seed, n_jobs=1, verbose=-1)
    model.fit(X, y)
    return model


def fit_sklearn_hist_gbm(X, y, seed=C.SEED):
    """Fallback only used when the official lightgbm package is unavailable."""

    model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=seed)
    model.fit(X, y)
    return model


def positive_scores(model, X):
    return np.asarray(model.predict_proba(X))[:, 1]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ cross-validation (C4)
def cross_validate_auc(prep, model_factory, n_splits=C.CV_SPLITS, seed=C.CV_SEED):
    """5-fold stratified CV with the scaler and SMOTE refit inside each training fold."""
    X = prep["X"].values
    y = prep["y"].values
    cont_idx = [prep["feature_names"].index(c) for c in prep["share_cols"]]
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=n_splits, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)
    fold_auc, fold_aux = [], []
    for k, (tr, te) in enumerate(skf.split(X, y), start=1):

        scores = positive_scores(model, Xte)

        fold_aux.append(

"""Optional explainability (SHAP, LIME), risk tiering and PSI monitoring.

These analyses are the paper's Section III-D/III-E and V-D machinery. They are
guarded so that the headline result (C1) never depends on them: any failure is
recorded as an error string in the metrics file instead of aborting the run.
"""

import numpy as np

import config as C


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ SHAP (R12)
def shap_global(prep, model, max_instances=None):
    """mean|SHAP| ranking for the LR primary model via shap.LinearExplainer (R12)."""
    import shap

    Xtr = prep["X_train_bal"]
    Xte = prep["X_test"]
    if max_instances is not None:
        Xte = Xte[:max_instances]
    explainer = shap.LinearExplainer(model, Xtr)
    values = explainer.shap_values(Xte)
    values = np.asarray(values)
    if values.ndim == 3:  # (n, p, classes)
        values = values[:, :, -1]
    mean_abs = np.abs(values).mean(axis=0)
    order = np.argsort(-mean_abs)
    ranking = [
        {"feature": prep["feature_names"][i], "mean_abs_shap": float(mean_abs[i])}
        for i in order
    ]
    return {
        "method": "shap.LinearExplainer",
        "n_instances": int(values.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(values.shape[1]),
        "top10": ranking[:10],
        "top1_share_of_total": float(mean_abs[order[0]] / mean_abs.sum()),
        "ranking": ranking,
    }


def linear_shap_fallback(prep, model, max_instances=None):
    """Analytic equivalent (phi_i = beta_i * (x_i - E[x_i])) used only if shap
    cannot be imported; noted as a fallback in the metrics file."""
    Xtr = prep["X_train_bal"]
    Xte = prep["X_test"]
    if max_instances is not None:
        Xte = Xte[:max_instances]
    phi = (Xte - Xtr.mean(axis=0)) * model.coef_.ravel()
    mean_abs = np.abs(phi).mean(axis=0)
    order = np.argsort(-mean_abs)
    ranking = [
        {"feature": prep["feature_names"][i], "mean_abs_shap": float(mean_abs[i])}
        for i in order
    ]
    return {
        "method": "analytic linear SHAP (shap unavailable)",
        "n_instances": int(Xte.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(Xte.shape[1]),
        "top10": ranking[:10],
        "top1_share_of_total": float(mean_abs[order[0]] / mean_abs.sum()),
        "ranking": ranking,
    }


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ LIME (R13)
def lime_local(prep, model, instance_indices, num_samples=2000, seed=C.SEED):
    """LimeTabularExplainer in classification mode with quartile-discretised
    continuous features and binary/one-hot columns declared categorical (R13)."""
    import lime.lime_tabular as lime_tabular

    names = prep["feature_names"]
    continuous = list(prep["share_cols"])
    categorical_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(names) if n not in continuous]
    explainer = lime_tabular.LimeTabularExplainer(
        training_data=prep["X_train_bal"],
        feature_names=names,
        class_names=["retained", "churn"],
        categorical_features=categorical_idx,
        discretize_continuous=True,
        discretizer="quartile",
        mode="classification",
        random_state=seed,
    )
    out = []
    for idx in instance_indices:
        exp = explainer.explain_instance(
            data_row=prep["X_test"][idx],
            predict_fn=model.predict_proba,
            num_features=6,
            num_samples=num_samples,
        )
        out.append(
            {
                "test_index": int(idx),
                "predicted_churn_probability": float(model.predict_proba(prep["X_test"][idx : idx + 1])[0, 1]),
                "top_features": [
                    {"rule": str(rule), "weight": float(w)} for rule, w in exp.as_list()[:6]
                ],
            }
        )
    return {
        "method": "lime.LimeTabularExplainer (quartile discretisation, classification)",
        "n_categorical_declared": len(categorical_idx),
        "instances": out,
    }

def _pkg_version(name):
    try:

def environment_info():
    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "platform": platform.platform(),

        "pandas": _pkg_version("pandas"),

def _round(obj, nd=6):
    if isinstance(obj, float):
        return float(round(obj, nd))
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: _round(v, nd) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [_round(v, nd) for v in obj]
    return obj


def gap(value, reference):
    return {
        "computed": _round(float(value)),
        "paper_reference": float(reference),
        "abs_gap": _round(abs(float(value) - float(reference))),

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- smoke
def run_smoke():
    t0 = time.time()
    os.makedirs(C.RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    csv_path = D.ensure_dataset()
    prep = D.prepare_smoke()
    checks = {}

    raw = D.load_raw(csv_path)

    checks["n_features"] = prep["info"]["n_features"]
    assert prep["info"]["n_features"] == C.EXPECTED_FEATURE_COUNT

    checks["n_balanced_train"] = prep["info"]["n_balanced_train"]
    assert prep["info"]["n_test"] == len(prep["y_test"]), "test partition resampled"

    model = M.fit_logistic_regression(prep["X_train_bal"], prep["y_train_bal"])
    scores = M.positive_scores(model, prep["X_test"])
    assert np.isfinite(scores).all(), "non-finite predicted probabilities"
    assert np.isfinite(model.coef_).all(), "non-finite coefficients"
    checks["n_coefficients"] = int(model.coef_.size)
    checks["n_intercept"] = int(np.size(model.intercept_))
    metrics = M.evaluate(prep["y_test"], scores)
    checks["auc_finite"] = bool(np.isfinite(metrics["auc_roc"]))
    assert metrics["auc_roc"] > 0.5, f"smoke AUC too low: {metrics['auc_roc']}"
    checks["smoke_auc_roc"] = metrics["auc_roc"]

    payload = _round(
